introduction.en: Critical minerals are essential components for modern technology, including renewable energy, defense, and electronics. Their strategic importance has led to comparisons with oil due to their role in powering the future economy.

body.en: The transition to green energy requires minerals like lithium, cobalt, and nickel. India faces challenges such as high import dependency, limited domestic exploration, and the dominance of a few countries in the global supply chain. To address this, India has formed KABIL to acquire assets abroad and is focusing on domestic exploration.

overview.title: Strategic And Critical Minerals
overview.definition: Strategic and critical minerals are non-fuel metallic or non-metallic minerals that are essential for the economic development and national security of a country, the supply chain of which is vulnerable to disruption.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Highly relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy - Industry, Infrastructure, Security, Environment) and Prelims (Geography, Economy, Science & Technology), focusing on India's net-zero transition, supply chain resilience, and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Strategic And Critical Minerals.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Critical Mineral Definition**: Minerals that are economically vital and whose supply chains are susceptible to disruption due to geopolitical concentration, monopoly, or scarcity.
• **Strategic Significance**: Essential for high-tech manufacturing, defense aerospace, telecommunications, and green energy technologies (EVs, solar panels, wind turbines, battery storage).
• **MMDR Amendment Act, 2023**: Landmark legislation empowering the Central Government to exclusively auction mining leases and composite licenses for **24 critical minerals**, removing them from the restrictive atomic or state-monopoly lists.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: India imports nearly 100% of its requirements for several critical minerals like Lithium, Cobalt, Nickel, and Platinum Group Metals, creating severe supply chain vulnerabilities.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Lithium, Cobalt, Nickel, Graphite, Rare Earth Elements (REEs). Found globally in Chile, Australia, DRC, China; limited domestic reserves in Jammu & Kashmir (Reasi) and Karnataka.
Driven by global decarbonization, EV adoption, and renewable energy storage requirements.
Crucial for Prelims (mineral locations) and Mains (Green Economy & Net Zero targets).
Titanium, Beryllium, Gallium, Germanium, Tantalum, Tungsten. Sourced globally via imports; minor domestic occurrences.
Critical for high-strength alloys, night-vision equipment, semiconductors, and radar systems.
Directly linked to National Security, Make in India in Defense, and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Silicon, Platinum Group Metals (PGMs), Vanadium, Niobium. Found in scattered geological formations.
Essential for electronics, catalysts, advanced telecommunications, and metallurgical hardening.
Important for Science & Tech integration with core economic geography.

items.definition: A Joint Venture company of three Public Sector Undertakings (NALCO, HCL, MECL) tasked with identifying, acquiring, developing, and processing strategic and critical minerals overseas (e.g., lithium projects in Argentina and Australia).
Institutional mechanism under the Ministry of Mines to continuously monitor global supply chains, domestic demand-supply gaps, and recommend policy actions.
A single license introduced via the MMDR amendments that grants both prospecting operations (exploration) followed seamlessly by mining operations to private and public sector bidders.
Proposed institutional framework to ensure end-to-end self-reliance, domestic exploration, recycling ecosystems, and strategic stockpiling of critical minerals.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Domestic Occurrences**: Lithium found in Salal-Haimana (Reasi, J&K) and pegmatites of Karnataka; Vanadium in Odisha; REEs in coastal monazite sands (Kerala, Odisha, AP).
• **Global Chokepoints**: China dominates rare earth processing (nearly 60-70% mining and 90% refining); Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) produces over 70% of global Cobalt; 'Lithium Triangle' in South America (Chile, Argentina, Bolivia).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High import dependence, technological deficit in deep-seated mineral extraction, environmental degradation, land acquisition bottlenecks, and geopolitical cartels.
• **Policy Interventions**: National Critical Minerals Strategy, 100% FDI under automatic route for mining and exploration of non-fuel and non-atomic minerals, Geological Survey of India (GSI) accelerated national mapping.

items.title: Mnemonic for India's 4 Core Battery & Tech Minerals
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "Li-Co-Ni-Graph" (Think: 'Likely Company Never Graphs').
• **Decoded Meaning**: **Li**thium, **Co**balt, **Ni**ckel, **Graph**ite.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly identifies the core quartet of energy transition minerals targeted in India's auction and KABIL acquisition portfolios.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: MMDR Act, 2023 deregulated **24** critical minerals and enabled **Private Sector** participation in atomic mineral exploration (except Uranium and Thorium restricted under state monopoly).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently misleads candidates by stating that all atomic minerals are completely barred from private sector mining. Post MMDR Amendments, certain atomic minerals (like Beryllium, Lithium-bearing minerals, etc.) have been removed from the strict atomic list to enable commercial exploitation.

Mains Value Addition: Use the framework of the 'Mineral Security Partnership (MSP)'—a US-led multi-national partnership where India is a member—to demonstrate how India is diversifying its critical mineral supply chains away from geopolitical concentration.

keyTakeaways: Critical minerals are the bedrock of the 21st-century green economy, renewable transition, and defense preparedness.
The MMDR Amendment Act, 2023 represents a paradigm shift by opening up 24 critical minerals to private exploration via composite licenses.
Global partnerships (KABIL, MSP) and domestic exploration via GSI are vital pillars to mitigate India's high import vulnerability.
